governing: plate shear rupture (J4.2, 0.6 Fu Anv / 2.00 = 54.8 kip vs 45.99 kip)
notes: Conventional single-plate per Manual Part 10, ASD. 5/16 in A572 Gr 50 plate x 12-1/2 in x 4-1/4 in wide, 4 rows of 3/4 in Group 150 (A490-N) snug-tight bolts in standard holes at 3 in pitch, Lev = Leh = 1-3/4 in on the plate, a = 2-1/2 in (1/2 in setback, 2 in beam edge, 1-3/4 in after underrun), top bolt 3-1/2 in below the beam top, 1/4 in E70 fillets both sides to the column web. Bolt group by the instantaneous-centre method with e = a/2 (Table 10-9): C = 3.66, 55.0 kip, utilisation 0.84; even with e = a the group is at 0.999. Other utilisations: block shear 0.76, plate shear yield 0.59, flexure 0.32 (M = V a), weld 0.50 direct / 0.52 eccentric, beam web shear 0.43. Every per-bolt bearing and tearout strength (plate and beam web, either direction) is at least the 15.0 kip bolt shear strength. Geometry: plate 12-1/2 in fits within the W18x35 T (15-1/2 in) and is at least T/2; plate t and beam web t are at most db/2 + 1/16; Leh is at least 2db on plate and beam; the 6 in beam flanges fit between the W10x49 flanges. The bolts sit between the column flanges, with about 4 in clear from the plate and beam web faces to the flanges, so snug-tighten them with a hand or right-angle wrench; pretensioning is not required. The column-web base-metal check (3.09 D / Fu = 0.19 in, less than 0.34 in) assumes no beam frames to the opposite side of the column web at this level. If one does, recheck the web with 6.19 D / Fu = 0.38 in, which is more than 0.34 in.
